answer: Only pools walked at low tide earn a seat, because the warden's book holds the starfish count of every tidepool along the shore. A wander count copied from another shore fails the book: at the violet of the pool the starfish must match the shore's own rocks, and a copied count belongs to another beach. Forging a season of counts means walking the pools for ninety mornings, bribing a warden and paying 8,200, while the whisper entry in the count book is read at every inspection, so a pool whose starfish were never counted is struck off.
